text:
maria: quick heads-up — UX conference week (May 12-16) traffic projection just landed. Our embedding + rerank traffic for search/personalization is expected to hit ~3x baseline during peak hours. Need a short ops plan for nightly batch reranks if batch pool saturates.

jamal: is that 3x from live clicks or from the precompute jobs?

maria: mix — ~2x live QPS, + additional 1x from more frequent nightly backfills (customers will run more queries). Forecast file: s3://infra-ops/forecasts/may-conference/embedding_rerank_v2.csv (linked).

sachin: rough numbers I pulled: baseline nightly batch = 150 GPU hours, baseline realtime = 50 GPU hours. Peak nightly could be ~450 GPU hours. Realtime headroom is tiny (~20% spare).

linh: oncall flag — we should avoid realtime pool overload during business hours. Can we prioritize live traffic and let batch spill to other options? :eyes:

maria: proposed options (short):
1) Short-term: enable spillover of batch jobs to spot-backed batch pool in us-west-2, with autoscale cap + preemption handler. Estimate cost +30% but keeps latency for users.
2) Medium: run partial batch rerank in smaller sharded batches over 48h window to flatten spikes.
3) Fallback: route overflow rerank queries to cheaper q4-quantized model on dedicated standby instances.

jamal: +1 to 1) but need network egress checks — some customers pinned to eu-west-1 cannot have data cross region. We should mark which customers are allowed to use spot spill.

sachin: adding cost math: if we spill 200 GPU hours/day to spot, expected cost delta = ~$5.6k/day (spot), vs $9.8k/day on on-demand. Savings but adds preemption risk. Also quantized model reduces GPU hours by ~40% but increases median rerank latency ~30ms.

linh: ops-bot ran quick health checks earlier — cluster slack in eu-west-1 is ~12% spare, us-east-1 ~8% spare, us-west-2 ~40% spare. ops-bot: `cluster-health --regions eu-west-1,us-east-1,us-west-2`

ops-bot: EU: 12% spare (preferred nodes: p4d-spot=0%), US-EAST: 8% spare (preferred nodes: a10g=20% reserved), US-WEST: 40% spare (spot friendly).

maria: ok. Actionable plan: 1) Allow nightly batch spill to us-west-2 spot pool for non-EU customers. 2) For EU-customer jobs, stagger batch into 3 windows (00:00, 04:00, 08:00 UTC) to smooth. 3) Temporarily enable quantized fallback for low-priority reranks. 4) Add alert: batch-spill-rate > 15% for >2h -> pager to eng-infra.

jamal: implementation notes: scheduler change -> set `rerank.batch.spill.enabled=true` and add `rerank.batch.spill.allowed_regions=["us-west-2"]` for team=non-eu in config. Small helm patch:
```
# values.yaml snippet
rerank:
  batch:
    spill:
      enabled: true
      allowedRegions: ["us-west-2"]
      maxSpillGpuHoursPerHour: 120
```

sachin: can we add a quick simulation run? I'll kick a synthetic spike against staging batch pools tonight (22:30 UTC) to validate autoscale + preemption handler.

linh: I'll own the alerting change (oncall). Will add the `batch-spill-rate` metric to the infra dashboard and set pager at 15% sustained.

maria: timeline: get helm patch reviewed by EOD, simulation tonight, enable spill for non-eu by tomorrow 06:00 UTC. If any region shows unexpected network egress > threshold, rollback.

jamal: FYI — we should also prime KV cache for top-queries before conference to reduce token cost. I'll open a short ticket for caching team.

maria: thanks all. tagging follow-ups: @jamal confirm helm PR, @sachin post simulation results, @linh dashboard + pager. :thumbsup:

sachin: simulation queued — will post results in this thread after run.

linh: alert created: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/embedding-rerank (dashboard link). Pager rule set.

ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary deploy of `rerank-scheduler v3.2.1` started (canary=2 pods)

maria: moving to close — follow-ups noted. If canary looks good, roll to prod at 04:00 UTC tomorrow.

sachin: simulation report: autoscale triggered at +2x, spot pool accepted 180 GPU hours, preemption rate 1.8% — good. Posting CSV results to s3.

jamal: helm PR merged.

linh: pager stayed silent during canary window. No regressed latencies.

maria: Excellent. I'll file a short postmortem-style runbook for this conference week and pin it to ops runbooks. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
